output.brief: The Android login drop is not caused by release 6.14. It comes from a new vendor rule, AUTO-LIB-17, that arrived with Corvane's 3 March rule-pack update. The rule blocks password-login requests from the app's networking library when no edge session cookie is present. It started blocking at 10:41 UTC on 3 March and returns HTTP 403. About 41,300 Android installs were blocked, and 92% of them had logged in successfully in the prior 90 days, so these are mostly real customers. The failures are identical across every app version, including old ones, and across OS versions, with or without the March security patch. Quick-unlock is unaffected. Password success fell from 96% to 8%. The evidence for credential-stuffing, the OS patch, the new password screen and the auth-token change is weak or counts against each. I'm fairly sure of this, though I haven't seen Corvane's confirmation or a test with the rule switched off. Next step: ask Corvane to set the new rule to log-only on the mobile password path, keeping the other edge protections, rate limits and lockout in place, then check that password-login success recovers. Don't roll back 6.14, raise bot sensitivity, or exclude blocked attempts from the KPI.
